customer_acme: Hey team — after rotating keys yesterday our API calls to /v1/generate are suddenly 401 invalid_api_key. We rolled back to the previous key but still getting 401. Debug logs attached below. Anyone seen this?

sara_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact Authorization header (redacted) and a curl you used? also which SDK/version? :eyes:

customer_acme: here's a sanitized curl from our CI log (we replaced the key body with Xs):

curl -v -H 'Authorization: ApiKey XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

We also tried the dashboard key tester and it works from our laptop, but CI and one server keep failing.

ben_devex: are you using any edge proxy or special encoding steps in your CI? sometimes CI runners inject env vars oddly.

customer_acme: CI runner is GitHub Actions self-hosted (Ubuntu). We fetch the key from a file: /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key and export it with: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(cat /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key)"

oncall_eng: can you paste the first 48 bytes of the file as hex? e.g. head -c 48 /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key | xxd -p -c 48

customer_acme: pasted output:
00000000: 2b2f 7b53 6b5f 4d6f 636b 79e2 80a2 200d  +/{Sk_Mocky.... 
00000010: 0a0d 2b41 2f3f 2d2b 0d0a 0000 0a0d 0a   ..+A/?-+......

sara_support: hmmm I see non-ascii sequences (e2 80 a2) and lots of CRLF sequences (0d 0a) in there. can you also run file -i /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key ?

customer_acme: file -i says: text/plain; charset=utf-7  :grimacing:  (weird, the file was generated by an old in-house key exporter)

oncall_eng: that explains it — the key file is encoded in UTF-7. Some editors/exporters historically wrote in UTF-7 and that will change the byte sequence sent in the Authorization header. The server expects the raw ASCII token bytes. When the header contains UTF-7 encoded bytes it fails auth with invalid_api_key (the token bytes don't match).

ben_devex: quick repro for others: create a file with the key then save it as UTF-7 and do:

# repro steps
printf '\uFEFF+/{Sk_MOCKKEY}\n' > utf7_key.txt   # saved with a UTF-7-capable tool in our test
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(iconv -f utf-7 -t utf-8 utf7_key.txt)"
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -v

You should see 401 and a hex dump will show the '+/' prefix and encoded sequences.

customer_acme: ok interesting. how did the dashboard tester succeed then?

sara_support: dashboard tester likely copies/pastes into the UI which normalized to UTF-8 or you tested from your laptop where you created a UTF-8 copy. CI file remained in UTF-7 so server saw different bytes.

oncall_eng: fix options: 1) re-encode the stored key file as UTF-8 without any BOM or extra chars: iconv -f utf-7 -t utf-8 /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key > /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key.utf8 && mv /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key.utf8 /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key && chmod 600 /etc/ci-secrets/redwood_key  2) rotate the key from dashboard and re-provision the new key into CI as an ASCII/UTF-8 file (recommended if you suspect partial corruption).

customer_acme: doing option 1 now — will test.

(10m later)

customer_acme: confirmed — re-encoding to UTF-8 fixed the CI job, calls succeeding again. Thanks! :tada:

ben_devex: great. we'll add a note to the troubleshooting docs about key file encodings and CI runners — small doc PR incoming.

sara_support: marking this resolved. leaving the thread for the docs PR and follow-up if you rotate keys. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Deployment #2024 of docs/troubleshooting/key-encoding-note scheduled for 2024-05-10 03:12 UTC

oncall_eng: quick follow-up advice for others — run a simple hex check on any key file pulled from automation: head -c 48 /path/to/key | xxd -p -c 48  — if you see bytes outside 20-7e range or BOM-like sequences, re-encode to UTF-8.

customer_acme: thanks everyone, saved our overnight run.
